skill.name: ux-prototyping
skill.description: Create interactive single-file HTML prototypes from UX specifications for validating user flows, screen states, and interaction patterns.
skill.summary: Build clickable HTML prototypes from UX specs for fast user-flow validation.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Most static external command and reconnaissance alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, and CSS border declarations. One medium risk is confirmed: the prototype template writes user-supplied item titles and descriptions into innerHTML without escaping, which can enable XSS in generated local prototypes. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md or assets/prototype-template.html.

remediation.issue: Unsafe item list rendering uses innerHTML with user-controlled fields.
remediation.suggestion: Render list rows with DOM creation and textContent, or escape title and description before assignment.

content.value_statement: UX specifications are hard to validate from static documents. This skill turns them into clickable HTML prototypes for faster review.
actual_capabilities: Reads a UX specification and extracts screens, states, journeys, and interactions.
Creates one self-contained HTML prototype with inline CSS and JavaScript.
Builds screen navigation with data-screen sections and simple state management.
Includes forms, modals, lists, tab navigation, empty states, and error states.
Provides a validation checklist for flow completion, feedback, and mobile responsiveness.
limitations: Generated prototypes are not production application code.
The default pattern uses local state and does not connect to real services.
Results depend on a clear UX specification or user-flow description.
Generated HTML should be reviewed before sharing or hosting publicly.

use_cases.title: Validate Product Flows
use_cases.description: Turn planned workflows into clickable prototypes before engineering starts.

use_cases.title: Review Interaction Design
use_cases.description: Convert screen and state notes into a prototype for design critique.

use_cases.title: Share Early Concepts
use_cases.description: Create a lightweight demo that stakeholders can open in a browser.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Prototype
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a documented UX spec.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an interactive HTML prototype from specs/architecture/ux.md. Include the main screens, navigation, and empty states.

prompt_templates.title: Prototype One Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when one journey needs validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a clickable prototype for the onboarding flow. Show success, error, loading, and back navigation states.

prompt_templates.title: Model Complex States
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for forms, modals, and data states.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this UX specification into a single-file prototype. Include modals, tab navigation, item creation, validation, and realistic sample content.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test UX
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced prototype from the UX spec. Cover primary, secondary, recovery, mobile, and edge-case flows for stakeholder review.

output_examples.input: A UX spec for account sign-up and onboarding.
output_examples.output: A browser-ready prototype with welcome, login, sign-up, home, settings, and responsive navigation screens.

output_examples.input: A product manager asks to test item creation.
output_examples.output: A clickable flow with an empty state, create modal, item list, detail view, and simple state updates.

output_examples.input: A design review needs mobile validation.
output_examples.output: A compact single-file prototype with realistic content, error states, loading placeholders, and a validation checklist.

best_practices: Provide a concise UX spec with main tasks, screens, states, and content.
Ask for one user journey at a time when the flow is complex.
Review generated prototypes for accessibility, text accuracy, and unsafe rendering before sharing.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the prototype as production-ready application code.
Do not omit error, empty, and loading states when validating workflows.
Do not paste sensitive real user data into prototype examples.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates single-file HTML prototypes for UX validation and user-flow review.

faq.question: Does it use external frameworks?
faq.answer: No. The documented pattern uses inline HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

faq.question: Can it work from any UX spec?
faq.answer: Yes, if the spec describes screens, states, interactions, and target flows.

faq.question: Is generated code production-ready?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for validation and should be reviewed before production use.

faq.question: Can it include mobile behavior?
faq.answer: Yes. The template and checklist emphasize responsive mobile validation.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
